facts.material: Styrofoam form covered with sisal fibers and cattail strands (plaiting materials, about 75% of surface), plus birch twig slices, straw, banana leaf, wooden twig, pine cone, plastic needles and eyes

gri_path: GRI 1: the figure is prima facie classifiable in several headings (4602 articles of plaiting materials, 3926 articles of plastics, 4421 wood) because it is a composite of different materials
GRI 3(a): each heading covers only part of the materials, so equally specific
GRI 3(b): the visible sisal and cattail plaiting materials covering about 75% of the surface give the owl its decorative appearance and essential character
GRI 6: 4602.19 of vegetable materials, other; not willow, rattan, bamboo, wickerwork; 4602.19.80.00 other

rejected_alternatives.reason: Styrofoam form is hidden and does not give the essential character
wood twig and slices are minor decorative accents
owl figure has no festive association
wickerwork line; the sisal and cattail covering is not wickerwork

classification.rationale: The owl is a composite good whose Styrofoam form is covered mostly (about 75 percent of surface) with sisal and cattail plaiting materials, which dominate its visual appearance and give it essential character under GRI 3(b). CBP classified a companion decorative hedgehog figure of the same construction in 4602.19.8000 (NY N362965, in force), and earlier sisal-covered animal figures likewise. It falls in the residual vegetable-material, non-wickerwork line 4602.19.80.00.
